Global (All).title: Tensions between US and China escalate over Taiwan
Global (All).summary: The US and China have been involved in a diplomatic row over Taiwan, with the US sending a delegation to the island and China issuing a warning against any official contact between the US and Taiwanese officials.

Global (All).title: Russia-Ukraine conflict continues with no signs of de-escalation
Global (All).summary: The conflict between Russia and Ukraine has been ongoing for several weeks, with both sides exchanging blows and no signs of a resolution in sight.

Global (All).title: Protests in Peru turn violent after presidential election results announced
Global (All).summary: Protests have broken out in Peru's capital city after the presidential election results were announced, with some turning violent and clashes between protesters and police reported.

United States.title: Gun Safety Bill Advances in U.S. Senate After Buffalo Shooting
United States.summary: A gun safety bill narrowly advanced in the U.S. Senate on Thursday, following a mass shooting in Buffalo

United States.title: Justice Department to Investigate Police Shooting of Janine Frost
United States.summary: The Justice Department announced on Thursday that it will investigate the fatal police shooting of Janine Frost

South Korea.title: Seoul's Han River bridge partially closed due to security concerns
South Korea.summary: A 20-meter section of the Cheongui-dong Bridge was closed on July 26 after authorities received a report of a suspicious object, but no explosive device was found.

South Korea.title: S. Korea to strengthen security cooperation with Mongolia for North Korea
South Korea.summary: South Korea said it will strengthen security cooperation with Mongolia to address regional threats posed by North Korea and bolster trilateral ties with the US.

South Korea.title: N. Korean defector found dead in S. Korea
South Korea.summary: A North Korean defector was found dead in a park in the southeastern city of Jinju, officials said, with the exact cause of death yet to be determined.

Japan.summary: Japan's government is considering revising its export control law to restrict shipments of semiconductor manufacturing equipment to China. The move is part of a broader effort to curb Chinese access to cutting-edge technology.

Typhoon Hinnamor made landfall in Japan on July 24, causing widespread power outages and injuring several people. The storm caused significant damage to buildings and infrastructure, particularly in the southern island of Kyushu.

A group of activists has released a video showing the alleged mistreatment of Japanese whaling ships in the Antarctic region. The footage appears to show the ships dumping large amounts of garbage and waste into the ocean, sparking outrage and condemnation from animal welfare groups and environmental organizations.
